description: Search inventory items. The query is matched against exact item codes / barcode labels first (e.g. "BM-002" printed on an asset tag), then as a name search. Name search is word-prefix based and casts a wide net ("Lap" matches all laptops), and a second accent-insensitive pass matches anywhere inside the name — "stuhl" finds both "Stühle" and "Bürostuhl". What it never does is SHORTEN your query, so the longer "Stühle" misses "Bürostuhl": search the shortest distinctive stem. An empty result [] means no match — retry with the most distinctive word. Every non-draft item HAS a category, so on an empty or weak result get the category tree from inventory_overview and filter by categoryId instead of guessing more names — that is how a human finds things here. The same move works for places and people: list_resources returns the location and people trees, and a node id from either goes straight into currentLocationId / currentHolderId. In results, `status` describes the item's CONDITION (available = not defect/lost/retired); a status-available item may still be borrowed — check `currentHolder`. To COUNT, read `trackingMode`: a row without it is one physical item (count rows), a "quantity" row is a stock pool (sum `quantity`). `primaryCode` is the code printed on the asset tag — the only way to tell two identical models apart. `webUrl` / `listUrl` open the record and the filtered list in the web app. These rows carry NO photo: when your user should SEE the result rather than hear it — several similar items, a choice to make — hand the ids you found to show_items, or to get_item for a single item, instead of reading rows back. Optional filters (combinable with search and each other): currentHolderId (pass "me" for items held by you, the key owner), categoryId, currentLocationId, status. categoryId and currentLocationId include the whole SUBTREE by default — a top-level category returns its subcategories' items, a building returns its rooms' items; pass categoryMatch / currentLocationMatch "exact" for that node alone. Omit all arguments to list newest items. Drafts (unreviewed captures, `isDraft`) are strictly personal: results only ever include the key owner's own drafts — other users' drafts are invisible to everyone (admins included), even by exact code or by id, until published.

categoryId.description: Filter by category id. Includes the whole subtree by default — see categoryMatch

categoryMatch.description: How categoryId matches. "subtree" (default) = that category AND all its subcategories, which is almost always what a person means. "exact" = only items filed directly on that category

currentHolderId.description: Filter by current holder: a person resource id, or the literal "me" for the key owner

currentLocationId.description: Filter by current location: a location resource id. Includes the whole subtree by default — see currentLocationMatch

currentLocationMatch.description: How currentLocationId matches. "subtree" (default) = that place AND everything inside it, so a building returns its rooms' items. "exact" = only items sitting on that place itself

search.description: Item code (exact match, e.g. BM-002) or name words (word-prefix plus accent-insensitive substring — use the shortest distinctive stem)

status.description: Filter by condition. "available" means not defect/lost/retired — the item may still be borrowed.

name: search_items

currencySums.description: Per-currency-field totals over EVERY matching row, not just this page — the answer to "what is this worth". Absent when the org has no currency field. A lower bound while `truncated` is true

label.description: Field label as the org named it

compartment.description: The compartment of that container the item sits in (absent = directly in the container)

container.description: The container this item is packed into, if any

effectiveHolder.description: Holder followed through the container chain

effectiveLocation.description: Location followed through the container chain

isDraft.description: Present and true only for an unfinished draft capture

modelId.description: The item's model — pass it as create_order lines[].modelId to order any instance of this model

primaryCode.description: The code printed on the item's asset tag — how a human tells two identical models apart. Absent when no code is attached

quantity.description: How many this row stands for — only on quantity-tracked pools. To count a pool, SUM this; to count serialized items, count rows

status.description: Condition: available | in_repair | defect | lost | retired ("available" means not defect/lost/retired — the item may still be borrowed)

trackingMode.description: "quantity" for a stock pool counted by amount. Absent = a serialized item, i.e. this row IS one physical thing

webUrl.description: Link to this item in the web app — give it to your user so they can look at the record themselves. Absent when the deployment has no public address configured

listUrl.description: Link that opens this same result in the web app. Absent when the filter combination has no list-URL form, or when the deployment has no public address

matchedBy.description: "code" when the query resolved as an exact asset code

note.description: Why an empty result is empty (e.g. no linked person for "me")

totalCount.description: Total matches (a lower bound when `truncated` is true)

truncated.description: The server scan hit its cap — narrow the search

title: Search items
